content:
HollyAnna CougarTracks DeCoteau Littlebull grew up with the mountains as her backyard, and later worked as a police officer on the roads near Wapato. She and her late husband, also an officer, traded stories they didn’t tell anyone else.

In this episode, HollyAnna recalls the night she and her cousins took a ride from a stranger on Track Road and noticed the driver had hooves instead of feet. Years later, on patrol, she picked up three girls who told her the same story, from the same stretch of road. She also tells of a boarded-up house with power it shouldn’t have had, screams from the field, and round objects thrown at her patrol car. A county worker who heard the screams with her left saying, “I don’t do Bigfoot.”

Her uncle taught her that Bigfoot is her brother: a protector who has looked out for her since childhood. She shares the snowballs thrown at her while she trained for biathlon, the round rocks left on her truck after she sang for her late husband, and the eyes at her window that set off her cat, also named Istieja.

The heart of the episode is HollyAnna’s account of a fast she took as a four-time cancer survivor, determined “to get to living or get to dying.” On the sixth night, as she sang, three figures appeared below her. They sang with her and clapped rocks along with her song. In the morning she found walking sticks and rocks left at the edge of her circle. She still keeps them.

“I’ve always been told that they are the caretakers of all living things. And if they die, so too do we.” — HollyAnna CougarTracks DeCoteau Littlebull
